notes.meaning: God gave Ezekiel a direct message to deliver to the people. Ezekiel did not invent these words or make them up from his own thoughts. Instead, he was acting as a faithful messenger delivering what the Lord revealed.

Ezekiel was commanded to speak against the prophets in Israel who claimed to represent God. These men were actually inventing their messages out of their own desires and wishful thinking. They told the people what they wanted to hear rather than what God had said.

God pronounced trouble on these foolish prophets. In the Bible, a foolish person is someone who leaves God out of their thinking and relies on themselves. These leaders followed their own human impulses and had never actually received a true vision from the Lord.

The Lord compared these dishonest prophets to foxes or jackals living among ruined walls. Instead of helping repair the nation, they scavenged among the rubble for their own benefit. They took advantage of a damaged people and only made the ruin worse.

When an ancient city wall broke during a battle, brave soldiers would stand in the gap to defend the people. True spiritual leaders do the same by praying, teaching truth, and urging people to turn from sin. These false prophets did nothing to help Israel stand strong before God's judgment arrived.

These prophets told lies and claimed that the Lord had spoken through them. Even though God had never sent them, they still hoped their words would come true. They had ended up believing their own deceptions.

God asked them directly if their visions and predictions were completely fake. They kept claiming that the Lord had spoken, yet He had said nothing to them. Using God's name to give authority to personal lies is an awful sin.

Because the prophets spoke empty words and made up visions, the Lord declared that He was against them. Prophets were meant to be close servants of God, but these men turned Him into their enemy. God promised that He would personally hold them accountable.

God laid out three punishments for these dishonest leaders. They would lose their place among the community leaders, their names would be blotted out of the family records of Israel, and they would never step foot in the land again. When this took place, everyone would recognize the supreme authority of the Lord.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: An older Catholic commentary mentions an interpretation where the writings of these false prophets would never be accepted into the sacred Scriptures.

notes.meaning: The false prophets misled the people by promising peace when real danger was right at the door. Ezekiel compared their work to workers putting a thin coat of whitewash over a poorly built wall. Instead of dealing with the nation's sins, they covered up serious weaknesses with cheerful words.

Ezekiel was told to warn the people that their badly built wall would soon collapse. God was sending torrential rain, huge hailstones, and fierce winds against it. This violent weather represented the Babylonian armies that would soon sweep through the land.

When the flimsy wall finally crashed down, onlookers would mock the false builders. People would ask what happened to the fine coat of plaster that was supposed to keep it safe. Hard testing quickly reveals whether our trust is built on truth or on empty promises.

The Lord confirmed that He would send the destructive wind, driving rain, and hail in His anger. The coming disaster was not random bad luck, but a storm directed by God Himself. His righteous anger would shatter every false source of safety.

God promised to knock down the whitewashed wall right down to its foundations. This meant the city of Jerusalem would fall, and the lying prophets would perish in its ruins. Through this severe judgment, the survivors would know that the Lord is the true God.

Once the storm had passed, the Lord would declare that both the wall and its plasterers were gone. Neither the false sense of safety nor the men who promoted it would survive. God completely removes what is built on deception.

This final destruction applied specifically to the prophets who promised peace to Jerusalem. They insisted everything would be fine when there was actually no peace at all. God warns that true peace cannot exist alongside unrepented sin.

God told Ezekiel to confront the women in Israel who were also making up prophecies from their own thoughts. The Lord had spoken through faithful women in Israel's history, such as Miriam and Deborah. But these particular women were pretending to be inspired by God when they were really speaking on their own.

These women practiced magical rituals, sewing charms onto wrists and placing veils on people of every height. They used these objects like nets to trap people and bring them under their influence for personal profit. They gave people a false feeling of security while leading them toward spiritual ruin.

These women insulted God's holy name for tiny payments like a handful of barley or small scraps of bread. Through their dishonest fortunes, they brought grief to the righteous and promised life to the wicked who were headed for death. They twisted spiritual truth just to make a cheap living.

The Lord announced that He was against the magic charms they used to trap people like birds. He promised to tear these superstitious bands from their arms and set the captive souls free. God defends ordinary people against spiritual predators.

God promised to tear away their magic veils and rescue His people from their control. The deceivers would no longer be allowed to prey upon the vulnerable with their occult practices. Through their defeat, they would learn that the Lord alone has real power.

These women had discouraged the righteous with lies, even though God had done nothing to bring them grief. At the same time, they encouraged the wicked to keep on sinning by falsely promising them safety. Godly teaching should encourage the faithful and call sinners to repentance, not the opposite.

Because of their wicked actions, the Lord would put an end to their false visions and fortune-telling. He would completely rescue His people from their grip. When this happened, everyone would know that He is the LORD.
